rationale: The MIN-based dual-market issuance requirement is a genuinely different financing construct from the archive's additive `sstk+dltis` version, though the conditioning leg is copied verbatim from Low Quality Equity Recapitalizer, so the incremental information is modest and it risks loading on the same net-external-financing anomaly.

target_name: Low Gross Quality Debt Funded Buyback
rationale: This is a cosmetic variant of the archive's best performer, Weak Cash Debt Funded Payout (fmb -3.64, ls_talpha -3.97) — identical MIN(debt issuance, payout) structure with oancf swapped for gross profit and dividends dropped — so it will be highly correlated with an already-evaluated signal rather than testing a new mechanism.

Replacing cash-flow volatility with cash-flow acceleration is a substantive shift from dispersion to directional deterioration and is internally consistent with the negative expected sign, but it reuses the identical financing leg from the failed Unstable Cash Financing Spike and ACCEL of an annual ratio is a noisy second difference, so the improvement odds are only moderate.

Near-rediscovery of Gross Profit Deterioration Security Issuer — same NEG(TREND(x/at,5)) × issuance structure, with sale/at mechanically nested inside gross-profit/at (which equals sale/at times gross margin) — so it is a minor decomposition of an already-tested signal rather than a new channel.

Substituting the liquidity *trend* for the level and requiring co-occurrence (MIN) of long-term issuance with short-term debt growth is a defensible restructuring of Liquidity Weak Debt Funding Stress, and the sign logic holds (DELTA(dlc) negative correctly pushes deleveragers to the bottom), though dropping the oancf term discards the leg most likely responsible for the prior version's alpha.

The construction is internally coherent and the MIN(buyback, debt reduction) requirement is a real refinement over the archive's crude buyback confirmation, but it is close to the sign-flipped complement of Weak Cash Debt Funded Payout and every long-side quality-payout variant in the archive has produced negligible FF5 alpha, so the prior for economic significance is low.
